Ninety seconds, three things, and I am starting with the one that is late. The price list rollout is running about a week behind. The bottleneck is the label supplier, not the plant, and we are splitting the order between two suppliers from Thursday. Second, the pilot. It is currently running in twelve workshops and the early numbers look good, better than we expected, but I am not calling it a success. I am waiting four more weeks, because the first month of a pilot always flatters itself. Third, the new distributor. That conversation is ongoing and nothing is signed. They are asking for a discount and we are not giving it, so we are talking about volume instead. One decision from this room today, and it is the label order. Everything else can wait a week.

Most status updates say nothing, and they say it at considerable length. What they are actually doing is listing activity. We are reviewing this, we are aligning on that, we are working with the agency. All true, all useless, and all it proves is that people are busy, which nobody doubted. A good update answers two questions and stops. What is different since last week, and what decision is somebody waiting for. If the answer to the first one is nothing, say nothing and give the time back. And one word I would delete from every status meeting in the world. Fine. A project is fine, and fine, and fine, right up to the week it is not, and then everybody is surprised except the person who knew in March. Fine is the most expensive word in the room.
